detail: Ford Motor Co. IPO: the Ford Foundation sold 10.2m shares at $64.50; 53.46m shares x first-day close $70.50 = $3.8bn.
Wal-Mart Stores IPO, 300,000 shares at $16.50 (OTC; NYSE from 1972-08-25).
Apple Computer IPO on Nasdaq: 4.6m shares at $22, first-day close $29 (reported valuation $1.78bn).
United HealthCare IPO on Nasdaq (date approximate; Yahoo history starts Oct 1984).
Microsoft IPO on Nasdaq at $21; first-day market value about $777m.
GE completes its purchase of RCA (era c records the event; value row added here: $6.28bn).
source: Wikipedia 'List of largest mergers and acquisitions' (retrieved 2026-11-12)

detail: Racal Telecom (later Vodafone) floats 20% of its shares in London (date approximate); fully demerged from Racal 1991-09-16.
Cisco Systems IPO on Nasdaq at $18.
Mitsui Bank absorbs Taiyo Kobe Bank (valued at $22.8bn in the 1989 deal; not tracked) to form Mitsui Taiyo Kobe Bank, renamed Sakura Bank in 1992.
source: Wikipedia 'List of largest mergers and acquisitions' (retrieved 2026-11-12)

detail: Pacific Telesis spins off its wireless arm AirTouch Communications (not tracked); PacTel cover value fell from $23.1bn (Feb 1994) to $12.7bn (Feb 1995).
Sears distributes its 80% of Allstate (not tracked).
GM splits off Electronic Data Systems (Class E stock, $27.6bn non-affiliate value in Feb 1996; not tracked).
Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz complete their merger into Novartis; Novartis end-1996 about $79bn (derived).
SBC Communications completes its purchase of Pacific Telesis (widely reported at about $16.5bn in stock; PacTel cover value Feb 1997 $17.6bn).
source: Pacific Telesis 10-K cover 1997 (SEC); deal value not re-verified

detail: Bell Atlantic completes its merger with NYNEX (NYNEX cover value Feb 1997 $22.6bn).
source: Wikipedia 'List of largest mergers and acquisitions' (retrieved 2026-11-12); NYNEX 10-K cover 1997

detail: Woolworth Corp. renamed Venator Group (1998), then Foot Locker Inc. (2001).

U S WEST separates its media business as MediaOne Group (Media Group tracking stock $18.0bn in Jan 1998; MediaOne was bought by AT&T Corp. in 2000; not tracked). Legally the old U S WEST Inc. became MediaOne and the telephone business continued as a new U S WEST Inc.; the vessel follows the telephone business.
SBC Communications completes its purchase of Ameritech ($62bn at the May 1998 announcement; Ameritech cover value Mar 1999 $72.8bn).
source: Wikipedia 'List of largest mergers and acquisitions' (retrieved 2026-11-12); Ameritech 10-K cover 1999

detail: Qwest Communications completes its purchase of U S WEST ($44bn at announcement; Qwest not tracked). US West value about $54.8bn on 2000-06-30 (CMC).
source: Wikipedia 'List of largest mergers and acquisitions' (retrieved 2026-11-12); companiesmarketcap.com/us-west/marketcap/

detail: Bell Atlantic completes its merger with GTE (not tracked) and renames itself Verizon Communications.
Mizuho Holdings listed (share transfer from the three banks); Mizuho end-2000 about JPY 8.2tn (derived).
Dow completes its purchase of Union Carbide (1.611 Dow shares per UCC share; $9.3bn in stock at the 1999 announcement, about $7.0bn at completion).
Sakura Bank (the former Mitsui Bank) merges with Sumitomo Bank into Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. (listed at $45.5bn in the M&A list).
source: Wikipedia 'List of largest mergers and acquisitions' (retrieved 2026-11-12)

detail: Tokai Bank and Sanwa Bank form UFJ Holdings (with Toyo Trust; not tracked).
Nomura Securities becomes Nomura Holdings (holding company).
Chevron completes its merger with Texaco (ChevronTexaco); Texaco about $38.4bn on the last day (CMC), $35bn deal value.
source: Wikipedia 'List of largest mergers and acquisitions' (retrieved 2026-11-12); companiesmarketcap.com/texaco/marketcap/

detail: Phillips Petroleum and Conoco (not tracked) combine under the new holding company ConocoPhillips (Phillips holders about 57%).

Kmart Holding (not tracked) buys Sears, Roebuck and both become subsidiaries of the new Sears Holdings Corp. (Kmart holders owned the majority); the sears vessel continues as Sears Holdings. Human decision: a new vessel would also be defensible.
AT&T Inc. (SBC) completes its purchase of BellSouth ($67bn in the M&A list).
source: Wikipedia 'List of largest mergers and acquisitions' (retrieved 2026-11-12)

detail: Matsushita Electric Industrial renames itself Panasonic Corporation.

General Motors Corp. files for Chapter 11; shares worth $457m on the last close (75 cents x 610m). The old equity was cancelled; the company became Motors Liquidation Co. The assets went to a new company (General Motors Company), owned by the US Treasury, Canada and the UAW trust.
source: Business Standard/Reuters 2009-06-02; Wikipedia GM Chapter 11 reorganization

detail: General Motors Company (new GM) re-lists on the NYSE at $33 (about $49.5bn; $20.1bn raised).

Eastman Kodak files for Chapter 11; shares 42-47 cents, about $114-128m. Kodak emerged in Sept 2013 with new shares issued to creditors (old shares cancelled); the new Kodak (KODK) is worth $0.3-1.5bn and is not tracked as a vessel.
ConocoPhillips spins off its refining business as Phillips 66 (not tracked; first CMC value about $20bn).
Nippon Steel absorbs Sumitomo Metal Industries ($22.5bn in the M&A list) and becomes Nippon Steel & Sumitomo Metal (renamed Nippon Steel Corp. 2019).
source: Wikipedia 'List of largest mergers and acquisitions' (retrieved 2026-11-12)

detail: Dow Chemical and E. I. du Pont merge into the new holding company DowDuPont (deal announced Dec 2015, $130bn in the M&A list); DowDuPont 2017-09-29: $161.7bn (CMC). Dow about $75bn and du Pont about $87bn at the merger (derived).
source: Wikipedia 'List of largest mergers and acquisitions' (retrieved 2026-11-12); companiesmarketcap.com/dupont-de-nemours/marketcap/

detail: Sears Holdings files for Chapter 11; shares at 32 cents, market value about $32m (Reuters).
DowDuPont spins off Dow Inc. (materials science); Dow Inc. first month-end about $42bn (CMC).
DowDuPont spins off Corteva (agriculture) and renames itself DuPont de Nemours, Inc.; Corteva first month-end about $20bn (CMC).
3M spins off its health-care business as Solventum (not tracked; first CMC value about $12bn).
Dick's Sporting Goods (not tracked) completes its purchase of Foot Locker (the former F. W. Woolworth Co.) for about $2.4bn.
source: Wikipedia Foot Locker (date and value not re-verified)
